sequence.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. This is a PRODUCTION2D painted sprite animation atlas, not concept art. Keep EXACT knight identity/clothes from the reference: brown short tousled hair, steel bronze armor, dark navy split tabard, brown gloves/boots, realistic proportional human. Camera orthographic shallow18-degree elevation, WHOLE character faces DIRECTLY AWAY from viewer (full BACK VIEW, facing north) IN EVERY SINGLE CELL. We see back of hair, rear armor and heels, NOT face or chest at any time. One rigid two-handed longsword; forward two-handed grip at chest height, NOT side guard. Same sword length, glove grip, anatomy and body height all cells. True clean transparent background. No colored fringe/no shadows/no text/no labels. LARGE TALL output2048x3840. Exact grid FOUR columns and ELEVEN rows,44 separate full-body poses, NO overlap across cells, plenty of margin for sword and falling body. Each row has4 figures, never skip a cell.
ROW1 four neutral idle breathing frames, relaxed straight legs, sword carried safely lowered.
ROW2 four combat idle breathing frames, two-handed forward guard.
ROWS3-4 eight-frame relaxed WALK LOOP, alternating left/right heel contacts, pass and toe off, subtle torso counter rotation, normal modest stride.
ROWS5-6 eight-frame COMBAT WALK LOOP with both hands retaining forward sword grip, knees flex naturally.
ROWS7-8 eight frames of ONE full-body TWO-HANDED DIAGONAL CUT: ready, hip/shoulder wind-up, backswing, step and beginning downswing, cut through, follow-through, recover, ready. Sword remains a rigid straight object, not wrist twirl.
ROW9 four HIT REACTION poses: struck shoulder, brief recoil, stable recovery, guard.
ROWS10-11 eight frames DEATH/FALL: struck, torso buckles, knees bend, one knee touches ground, side hand reaches floor, body falls sideways, lands, final body lying still. NO blood. Full silhouette all cells, no cropping lying body. Fixed rear facing even during movements.
Output ONLY complete44figure atlas, painterly brushwork and crisp detailed shapes matched to input, each cell body about260px tall at standing.

showcase.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production hand-painted2D tactical RPG animation sprite atlas matching the supplied knight EXACTLY. Young adult human knight, short tousled chestnut hair, clear clean-shaven face, engraved steel and bronze armor, dark navy split tabard with restrained gold hem, brown gloves and proportional brown boots. One long rigid straight two-handed sword. BOTH hands around the SAME hilt in forward combat guard with diagonal upward blade, hands projected in front of chest; NEVER beside shoulder in a side guard. Orthographic shallow18-degree elevated camera, facing DIRECT BACK, entirely facing away, see back of hair and rear armor, no face or chest. Keep that view throughout ALL24cells, same identity, head/body size, costume, materials and lighting. One straight rigid sword of identical real length, two gloved hands on its hilt in ready/fighting poses, proportions/sensible boots unchanged. True clean transparent background, no floor/shadow/text/labels/neon fringe. Exact4 COLUMNS by6 ROWS,24 full-body poses, generous separated cells, no cropped blade/feet. Large portrait output1536x2304.
ROW1 FOUR DRAW frames: relaxed with sword in hip scabbard, right glove grasps hilt while left steadies scabbard, right shoulder/arm draws sword clear, both gloves take the SAME hilt in forward diagonal-upward combat guard A.
ROW2 FOUR SHEATHE frames: guard A, lower/alignment of blade to scabbard mouth with right hand and left steadying scabbard, slide blade in, relaxed sheathed stance.
ROWS3-4 EIGHT frames of one TWO-HANDED THRUST: forward guard A, hips/shoulders coil drawing hands back, bend elbows/chamber, short step begins, torso/arms extend sword point toward facing/target, maximum full-body thrust, retract with weight recovery, original guard A. Target straight AWAY FROM CAMERA/TOP CENTRE: end-on blade foreshortened ahead of torso near centre, no long left/right sideways sword. Hilt never leaves both hands, shaft/blade remains rigid. No wrist twirling.
ROW5 FOUR PARRY frames: original forward guard, both hands raise blade across incoming line, brace using shoulders/hips with slight knee flex, recover guard.
ROW6 FOUR short DODGE/BACKSTEP frames: guard A, rear foot pushes back and knees flex, controlled short backward evasive step with torso leaning slightly away, recover guard. No huge leap or cartoon squash, no whole-cutout translation. Body articulates naturally.
